          Arsenal Ease Pressure, Chelsea Take Top Spot, and Man City’s Perfect WSL Start Ends: Five Talking Points From Matchday 7
        
      
                          
                      Oct 26, 2026
          
                      Maya Shah / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
The WSL title race took an intriguing turn as Chelsea capitalised on Man City’s dropped points, Arsenal found much-needed respite with a derby-day triumph over Tottenham, Aston Villa continued their upward trajectory, and Liverpool denied London City Lionesses another victory.
Matchday 7 brought another significant shift in the WSL landscape, with plenty of talking points across the division.

Arsenal finally ended their frustrating wait for a league victory, overcoming Tottenham in the north London derby to claim their first win since the opening day and ease some of the pressure on their faltering campaign.
Elsewhere, Manchester City’s perfect start was ended by cross-city rivals Manchester United, allowing Chelsea to move top of the table for the first time this season.

Sonia Bompastor’s side, however, had to work harder than expected to take advantage, coming from behind at half-time to beat Crystal Palace. It marked the first time under the French manager that Chelsea had overturned a half-time deficit against an opponent outside the traditional elite (Arsenal, Man City and Man Utd).

Aston Villa, meanwhile, secured consecutive league victories for the first time since the end of the 2024-25 season, while Liverpool fought back to earn a point against London City Lionesses, bringing their opponents’ record-breaking winning streak to an end.
Here are our biggest takeaways from the latest round of action.
Chelsea are top of the WSL for the first time this season after surviving a stern examination from Crystal Palace and producing a late turnaround to claim all three points.
The Blues’ French contingent proved decisive, with Melvine Malard at the heart of the comeback. However, the result was far from straightforward.

Molly Bartrip’s opener was a landmark moment for the Eagles, representing the first goal Crystal Palace have ever scored against Chelsea. It also placed the Blues in an unfamiliar position: trailing at half-time against a promoted side.

Chelsea had conceded the opening goal to a promoted team on only four previous occasions in WSL history, with the most recent instance coming in May 2023, when Liverpool took the lead before Chelsea recovered to win 2-1.

Palace, however, will be disappointed by their inability to maintain their advantage. They have now conceded six goals in the final 15 minutes of WSL matches this season, the highest total in the division.
Malard was the standout performer as she recorded five shots on target, equalling the highest individual tally in a WSL match this season alongside Lauren Hemp and Khadija Shaw.

Her opening goal was particularly spectacular, marking only the third time she has scored from outside the box in the WSL and her first such effort since the beginning of last season, when she found the net against Leicester City.

The French striker was a constant presence in dangerous areas, recording more touches inside the opposition penalty area than any other player over the weekend (15). She also accumulated 1.7 xG, the highest total of her WSL career. Despite her impressive performance, the French forward may feel she could have added further goals to her tally.

The comeback was also shaped by the quality of Chelsea’s wide play. Katie McCabe recorded 34 successful passes ending in the final third, more than any other player across the weekend, illustrating her influence in sustaining pressure around Palace’s defensive block.

Sandy Baltimore proved effective from the bench, embarking on an incisive run and delivering the ball into a dangerous area for Malard's second, while her penalty sealed a 3-1 away victory for Bompastor's side.
Malard's brace made her only the second French international in Chelsea’s history to score more than once in a WSL match, following Baltimore’s achievement in January earlier this year.
The result was a significant one for Chelsea, who have now capitalised on Manchester City dropping points to move to the top of the table.

Arsenal delivered a much-needed result, coming from behind to defeat Tottenham 2-1 in the north London derby and ending their five-match winless run in the WSL. The victory marked the first time the Gunners had overturned a deficit to win a league match since September 2025, when they defeated West Ham 5-1.
